The case centers on the Hong Kong Alliance, which organized the vigils for about three decades, and leaves the three activists facing lengthy imprisonment for conduct linked to the group’s activities after the law took effect.

stories.title: Far-Right AfD Achieves Significant Victory in Saxony-Anhalt State Election
stories.summary: The Alternative for Germany (AfD) party secured a notable victory in the Saxony-Anhalt state election, receiving 44% of the vote, just shy of an absolute majority. This marks the most significant success for a far-right party in Germany since the Nazi era. Despite the win, the AfD fell three seats short of a majority and faces challenges in forming a government due to mainstream parties' refusal to collaborate with them. The outcome has prompted discussions about potential political shifts in Germany.
stories.event_title: Germany's AfD Party Poised for Historic State Election Victory

story_report.summary: In Saxony-Anhalt’s September 6 state election, the preliminary count put Alternative for Germany at 43.8% of second votes and 39 seats in the 83-member Landtag, three short of the 42 needed for an absolute majority. The result makes AfD the first far-right group to come close to regional power since World War II. Its leaders have begun seeking support to govern, but the CDU has reaffirmed it will not cooperate, leaving the formation of a government unsettled.

Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin and North Korean Premier Pak Thae-song initiated traffic by video link, Russia’s Transport Ministry said. The two-lane Yakov Novichenko bridge is about one kilometre long and can carry up to 300 vehicles daily; trucks may use it immediately. Its opening adds a road link as bilateral ties have strengthened since the Ukraine conflict began.
